title: NFR
description: AI-first non-functional requirement: a measurable quality constraint, separate from functional requirements per the IEEE 830 load-bearing-separation finding and referenced by requirement.nfr_refs by id. An NFR binds a metric to a target with a defined measurement, traces to a system-foundations node (or other service-design provenance), and carries its own verification acceptance so it is checkable, not prose. Part of the definition layer (legion #526); shape validated against live NFRs (mail, gitpress).

category.description: Quality-attribute class (ISO/IEC 25010-aligned). compliance covers protocol/RFC conformance.

metric.description: The measurable quantity this NFR constrains, e.g. 'IMAP IDLE re-issue interval' or 'DKIM signing latency p99'

target.description: Human-readable threshold, e.g. '< 29 minutes' or '< 200ms p99'

bound.description: Machine-checkable form of target. Optional but preferred -- lets the verify gate assert numerically.

max.description: Upper bound when comparator is range

measurement.description: How the metric is observed/verified, e.g. 'integration test asserts IDLE re-issued before 29:00' or 'prometheus histogram dkim_sign_seconds'

traces_to.description: Provenance: a system-foundations blueprint node (e.g. blueprint.system-foundations.protocol-compliance.rfc-3501), moment_of_truth.<id>, journey phase, or pain theme. Required -- no orphan constraints.

applies_to.description: Requirement ids or surface names this NFR constrains (the inverse of requirement.nfr_refs)

verification.description: How this NFR is verified. acceptance is the checkable-criteria source the verify gate (#520) reads when the NFR is bound; tests pins test names or file:line once implementation exists.
